items.description: San Jose's historic central market is a busy place for food, shopping, and daily city life. It remains one of the capital's most authentic public spaces.
Costa Rica's National Theatre is the country's best-known cultural building and a symbol of coffee-era wealth. It anchors the artistic life of downtown San Jose.
A traditional coffee finca in Costa Rica's highlands, shaped by volcanic soil and cool mountain air. Coffee farming here is both an economic activity and a cultural identity.
A weekly farmers market where local producers sell fresh fruit, vegetables, and regional foods. It connects rural agriculture directly with urban consumers.
Sarchi is known across Costa Rica for colorful oxcarts and woodcraft. The town's artisan work is one of the country's strongest craft traditions.
Traditional corn tortilla making remains a daily habit in Guanacaste and other parts of Costa Rica. The comal and hand-formed dough keep the practice rooted in home cooking.
Boruca masks are hand-carved indigenous artworks from southern Costa Rica. They are closely tied to the Diablitos tradition and community identity.
Gallo pinto is Costa Rica's best-known everyday dish, made from rice and beans. It is especially associated with breakfast and national food culture.
Balsa wood crafts show how light local materials can become decorative art. The carved figures and souvenirs are common in markets and workshops.
The Limon Carnival fills the Caribbean city with parades, music, and Afro-Caribbean energy. It is one of the most visible celebrations of local identity in Costa Rica.
Chorotega pottery is a long-standing artisan tradition centered around Guaitil and Nicoya. The clay vessels and painted finishes keep indigenous knowledge alive.
Pineapple farming is one of Costa Rica's most important export crops. Large plantations in warm lowland regions feed both domestic markets and international buyers.
Traditional fishing villages along the coast still follow the tide and the daily catch. Their routines are shaped by small boats, nets, and close ties to the sea.
Costa Rica's yoga and wellness retreats combine tropical scenery with rest and mindfulness. They are a major part of the country's modern nature-based tourism.
The Bribri cocoa tradition links cacao to indigenous knowledge on the Caribbean side of Costa Rica. It includes ritual drinks, farming skills, and local heritage.
